topic.title: Naming Conventions
topic.description: Standard conventions for naming in Java

sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Naming things in Java isn't just about creativity - it's about clarity! Let's master the rules that make your code speak for itself.

• Why naming conventions matter in Java
• How to name variables, methods, and classes correctly
• Common mistakes to avoid (and how to fix them)

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine you're organizing a toolbox. You wouldn't mix up screwdrivers and wrenches with random labels - you'd use clear, consistent names so you can find what you need instantly. Java naming conventions work the same way!

Java has simple rules to make your code readable:

• **Variables & Methods**: Start with lowercase, then camelCase for multiple words
  - ✅ `studentName` (good) vs ❌ `StudentName` (bad)
  - ✅ `calculateTotal()` vs ❌ `CalculateTotal()`

• **Classes**: Start with uppercase, then camelCase
  - ✅ `StudentRecord` vs ❌ `studentRecord`
  - ✅ `BankAccount` vs ❌ `bank_account`

• **Constants**: ALL_UPPERCASE with underscores
  - ✅ `MAX_SIZE` vs ❌ `maxSize`

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Avoid $ and _ in regular names (reserved for special cases)

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Keep names short but meaningful (e.g., `avg` vs `averageScore`)
donts: Don't use spaces or special chars (e.g., `student-name`)
sections.protip: When in doubt, ask: 'Will someone else understand this name instantly?' If not, rename it!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Naming conventions aren't just academic - they're used everywhere:

examples.how: Follows strict naming like `onClickListener()` (method) and `R.layout.activity_main` (resource reference)
Consistent naming makes collaboration easier (e.g., `isValidEmail()` vs `checkEmail()`)

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Naming conventions make your code readable and professional
📌 Practice by fixing bad names in existing code
📌 You're now ready to write clean, convention-following Java code!
